Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.


```{r}
library(airway)
library(DESeq2)

data(airway)
airway
```

```{r}
# pull the count matrix out of the SummarizedExperiment
counts <- assay(airway, "counts")

# select rows 1:5 and column 1:4

counts[1:5, 1:4]

#counts dimension

dim(counts)

#Total reads per column (or per sample)

colSums(counts)

```


```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(tibble)

sample1_counts <- counts[, "SRR1039508"]

# distribution of counts acroos all genes in one sample

ggplot(tibble(count = sample1_counts), aes(x = count)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 100)+
  labs(title = "Counts across all genes in SRR1039508",
       x = "raw count", y = "number of genes")
  
  
```

```{r}
#The first fix to such a skewed data is to log transform the values

ggplot(tibble(count = sample1_counts), aes(x = count+1)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 100)+
  scale_x_log10()+
  labs(title = "Counts across all genes in SRR1039508",
       x = "raw count", y = "number of genes")
```

```{r}
# pick a moderately expressed gene
gene_id <- "ENSG00000000003"   # TSPAN6
gene_counts <- counts[gene_id, ]
gene_counts

```



```{r}
gene_means <- rowMeans(counts)
gene_vars  <- apply(counts, 1, var)

mv_data <- tibble(mean = gene_means, variance = gene_vars)

ggplot(mv_data, aes(x = mean+1, y = variance+1)) +# +1 pseudocount only for log-axis display; not used in analysis
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2, size = 0.5) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, color = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(title = "Mean-variance relationship across all genes",
       subtitle = "red dashed line: variance = mean (Poisson)",
       x = "mean count (log10)", y = "variance (log10)")


```
Down with dex (anti-inflammatory effect — proinflammatory targets):

IL6 — proinflammatory cytokine, classic GR-suppressed target
PTGS2 (COX-2) — proinflammatory enzyme, NF-κB target, GR-suppressed
CCL2 (MCP-1) — chemokine, NF-κB target

Up with dex (direct GR transactivation targets):

DUSP1 (MKP-1) — this is a textbook GR-induced gene
FKBP5 — GR pathway feedback, very strongly induced by dex
TSC22D3 (GILZ) — anti-inflammatory effector induced by GR
KLF15 — transcription factor induced by GR
PER1 — circadian gene strongly induced by GR

Unchanged (housekeeping):

ACTB (β-actin)
GAPDH
